newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Manila defence chief confident of bid for president.
newsitem.headline: Manila defence chief confident of bid for president.

text.p: Outgoing Philippine Defence Secretary Renato de Villa said on Tuesday he is confident of winning the ruling party's nomination for 1998 presidential elections despite his low standing in opinion polls.
"Let's just say I am confident I can make it," De Villa said when asked about his chances of winning the ruling party's nomination.

Seven people, including Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo and the president's sister, Senator Leticia Ramos-Shahani, have said they would contest the nomination, he told reporters during a brief visit to Singapore.
De Villa, who is resigning from the Defence Department on September 15, said it was vital for the "good policies and programmes" of President Fidel Ramos to continue.
"The matter of continuity, especially in our economic policies, would provide us great advantage in pursuing our national goals," he said.
"The challenge has become bigger and the importance of having someone succeed the President has become much greater."

The former armed forces chief trails badly in opinion polls behind former actor and Vice-President Joseph Estrada in the run-up to the elections, but analysts in Manila said he is banking on the support of Ramos to win.
De Villa was in Singapore as part of a farewell call on his counterparts in neighbouring countries.
He had a 40-minute meeting with Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and also met Defence Minister Tony Tan.
The Philippine official said Goh was "very much enthused" about the progress in bilateral relations between the countries.
The Singapore Defence Ministry said in a statement "defence relations are an important part of the broad-based relationship between Singapore and the Philippines."
